preconditions.description: The number of nodes n in the input tree is between 2 and 10^5 inclusive.
The input contains exactly n-1 edges defining the tree structure.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and u != v for u, v in edges)
preconditions.description: All edge endpoints are valid distinct node indices within the range [1, n].
The input edges form a valid connected tree (acyclic and connected).

postconditions.description: The number of printed decomposition nodes matches the integer m.
The number of printed edges in the decomposition tree is exactly m-1.
The union of all node sets in the decomposition covers all nodes of the original tree.

postconditions.expression: all(any(u in bag and v in bag for bag in bag_sets) for u, v in edges)
postconditions.description: For every edge in the original tree, there exists a decomposition node containing both endpoints.

postconditions.expression: all(all(node in bag for node in path_bags) for node in range(1, n + 1) for path_bags in paths_containing_node(node, bag_sets, decomp_edges))
postconditions.description: For every node in the original tree, the set of decomposition nodes containing it forms a connected subtree in the decomposition tree.

postconditions.expression: max(len(bag) for bag in bag_sets) == min_weight
postconditions.description: The maximum size of any bag in the decomposition equals the minimum possible weight (optimal T-decomposition).
The number of nodes m in the decomposition is the minimum possible among all decompositions achieving the optimal weight.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= m and 1 <= v <= m and u != v for u, v in decomp_edges)
postconditions.description: All decomposition edges reference valid distinct node indices within the range [1, m].
